slides.heading: Reverse Linked List
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Reverse Linked List, a hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Reverse in place and return the new head.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Reverse in place and return the new head.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Flip each link to point backwards, keeping three pointers so nothing is lost.
slides.narration: Flip each link to point backwards, keeping three pointers so nothing is lost.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Copy into array, rebuild → O(n) space
slides.narration: Rebuilding from an array uses extra memory. The iterative version flips one pointer at a time with prev, current and next.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Save next, point current at previous
slides.narration: Step by step. First, previous starts null. Second, save next, point current at previous. Third, advance both. Fourth, previous is the new head.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: While head isn't null, save next, point head at prev, move prev to head and head to next. Return prev.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Save next before you overwrite the pointer, and return prev at the end.
